rationale: The hypothesis posits that ascertainment bias explains seizure penetrance in GTF3C3-related neurodevelopmental disorder, predicting that cohorts ascertained for syndromic intellectual disability and dysmorphism exhibit <=50% seizure penetrance compared to >80% in developmental and epileptic encephalopathy cohorts. While Abdel et al. (2025) identified biallelic GTF3C3 variants through GeneMatcher in a cohort evaluated primarily for microcephaly, developmental delay, and dysmorphic facies with seizures in only 50% (2/4), De Hayr et al. (2025) characterized a cohort ascertained primarily for syndromic autosomal recessive intellectual disability and dysmorphic features across 12 patients and reported seizures in 11/12 (91.7%). Because a large syndromic intellectual disability cohort demonstrates >90% seizure penetrance, ascertainment mode alone cannot cleanly account for the lower penetrance observed in Abdel et al.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 12 affected individuals from 7 families characterized for a novel autosomal recessive intellectual disability syndrome with variable facial features and brain malformations, seizures were present in 11 of 12 patients (91.7%).

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 result in an autosomal recessive disorder with intellectual disability
source.quote: Twelve affected individuals from 7 unrelated families were identified with homozygous or compound heterozygous missense variants in GTF3C3... The cohort presented with intellectual disability, variable nonfamilial facial features, motor impairments, seizures, and cerebellar/corpus callosum malformations... Consistent to seizures seen in 11/12 patients

evidence.text: In four patients from three unrelated families ascertained through GeneMatcher presenting with microcephaly, developmental delay, intellectual disability, and dysmorphic facies, seizures were documented in 2 of 4 (50%) individuals.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: The patients exhibited microcephaly, developmental delay, intellectual disability and distinctive dysmorphic facies that appear recognizable in very young children... Seizures were observed in half of the patients.

evidence.text: GTF3C3 was identified as a candidate disease gene within a targeted cohort of 63 patients specifically recruited for early-onset epileptic encephalopathy (EE) and developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE).

source.title: The role of recessive inheritance in early-onset epileptic encephalopathies: a combined whole-exome sequencing and copy number study
source.quote: We further support candidacy for neurodevelopmental disorders of four previously described genes (PIK3AP1, GTF3C3, UFC1, and WRAP53)... increased in our epileptic encephalopathy cohort

conflicts: De Hayr et al. (2025) ascertained patients primarily for intellectual disability and syndromic neurodevelopmental features, yet observed an 11/12 (91.7%) seizure frequency, directly conflicting with the hypothesis that syndromic ID cohorts exhibit <=50% penetrance.

Abdel et al. (2025) identified seizures in only 2 of 4 (50%) patients gathered through GeneMatcher for microcephaly and dysmorphic facies, showing intra-phenotypic variability rather than a consistent dichotomy based on ascertainment source alone.

new_directions.question_text: Does variant position or residual TFIIIC complex activity correlate with the age of onset and severity of seizures in GTF3C3-deficient individuals?
new_directions.rationale: Differences in seizure penetrance between 11/12 in De Hayr et al. and 2/4 in Abdel et al. may reflect genotype-phenotype correlations (e.g., missense variants disrupting specific TFIIIC protein-protein interfaces vs. truncation alleles) or age-dependent penetrance rather than recruitment bias alone.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true lifetime cumulative incidence of unprovoked seizures in patients with biallelic GTF3C3 variants tracked prospectively beyond early childhood?
new_directions.rationale: Patients reported without seizures in pediatric cohorts may be pre-symptomatic at the time of publication, confounding ascertainment analysis.
